verdict.rationale: Raygun documents an official MCP server and a v3 OpenAPI-specified API for accessing Raygun data. It captures full stack traces, ranks errors by users affected and occurrence count, and offers an error-status workflow for triage, so an agent can plausibly pull and triage top issues. However, nothing shows which error or stack-trace data the API or MCP tools actually expose, and there is no documented issue-tracker integration for filing bugs. missing for 10: documentation that the MCP server/API returns top issues with stack traces, programmatic status/triage operations, native filing of bugs into a tracker (e.g. Jira/GitHub Issues), hands-on corroboration of an agent workflow.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, an agent can pull my top production issues with stack traces via API or MCP, triage them, and file the real bugs into my tracker

citations.quote: allows you to access your Raygun data so that you can display, manipulate and process it in other tools, scripts and applications.
Raygun automatically captures detailed diagnostics for each and every error occurrence including full stack traces
Order and prioritize errors based on users affected and the number of occurrences
Error statuses provides a workflow for triaging and managing your error inbox in Crash Reporting.
